current_flow: Today: task 1 emits periodControl on every successful data answer and task 2 built continueTurn(turnId, question, selection) plus per-turn id/isPending/error, and PROVED the deterministic continuation. ask-panel.tsx renders periodChoice for a clarification (:141-167, including turn.isPending and turn.error) but has ZERO references to periodControl, and SuccessAnswer (:193) receives only `response`. The panel locks suggestions and composer from the global isPending; use-ask.run trims the question before storing it on the turn (:86); continueTurn refuses while isPending by returning false (:98).
summary: Cold read of the ask-period-control-on-answers contract. Six findings, five of them mine to fix and one put to the human. The sharpest was that my own 'exactly as typed' guarantee was already false - use-ask.ts:86 trims on every path - so the criterion could never have failed honestly. The read also found the contract assigned nobody to render the pending and failure state continueTurn already sets, which would have made a failed period switch silent, and that two of the proposed leaves could pass against the wrong implementation: a click leaf asserting only the API request cannot tell continueTurn from a direct api.ask, and a no-control leaf whose fixtures omit periodControl passes a renderer that ignores responseClass entirely.
gaps: The exact-question guarantee was already false: use-ask.ts:86 stores question: trimmed on EVERY path, so 'stays exactly as typed' could never hold and the criterion was unfalsifiable as written.

C7 had no UI owner for settled answers: continueTurn sets turn.isPending and turn.error, but SuccessAnswer (ask-panel.tsx:193) takes only `response`, so a period switch would have shown neither that it was working nor why it failed.

The settled global-lock decision was not carried into nested controls: the panel disables suggestions and the composer from the global isPending (ask-panel.tsx:72,110), but a control on a second answer would have stayed clickable, been silently rejected by continueTurn (use-ask.ts:98 returns false), and given the user no feedback.
The click leaf could falsely prove the wrong implementation: an assertion only on the eventual API request cannot distinguish continueTurn from a prohibited direct api.ask call.
The 'no control' leaf needed adversarial fixtures: AskResponse is a flat optional interface, so a renderer that ignores responseClass passes any fixture that merely omits periodControl.

The control's UI shape was unspecified and accessibility-critical: .ask-options styles only unselected pill buttons and offers no selected state, while a settled answer must show WHICH period it is on.

Two of the contract's acceptance criteria were PROCESS, not product: the design-skill attestation and the proof discriminator plus tests.json status. A product diff cannot evidence either - their evidence lives in .factory/tests.json, which review excludes as harness bookkeeping - so the quality lens could only ever read them as partial, and it did, blocking the close twice.
resolutions: HUMAN ROUND: narrow the claim to what is true. The guarantee is now 'a period switch never CHANGES the question' - turn.question passes to continueTurn untouched - and the contract states plainly that the turn was trimmed once at ask time, so nobody later believes a stronger promise. Preserving the raw question end-to-end was rejected as widening this task into the shared ask path for a whitespace difference.

A criterion now requires SuccessAnswer to receive the turn and render turn.isPending and turn.error, mirroring the clarification branch at ask-panel.tsx:141-167. This is presentation of state that already exists, not new state, so it stays inside the three-file scope and task 2's sealed stage is not reopened.
A criterion now requires the control to be disabled while the panel is globally pending, matching ask-panel.tsx:72,110.

The click leaf must also prove the continuation behaviour reaches the SCREEN - targeted in-place pending, the previous answer retained, and a visible failure - which a direct api.ask call cannot produce. Split across two leaves so each failure mode is named.
The no-control leaf must use fixtures that DELIBERATELY carry a periodControl on informational, clarification and failure classes.

The control is specified as a compact labelled native <select> ('Period') bound to periodControl.current - a real selected entry, keyboard and screen-reader behaviour for free, and it fits the 360px dock without competing with the result. Decided here rather than asked: emil-design-eng and frontend-design are mandatory on this task precisely to make that call.

Both are removed from acceptance_criteria and plan_contracts. Neither is lost: record_test_from_json.py already REFUSES a user_facing artifact whose skills_used omits emil-design-eng or frontend-design, and check_task_proof.py already enforces the tests.json status, so the harness enforces them where they belong. The methodology stays in the task contract prose and, for the part a future author actually needs, in a note at the top of the test file - with no claim about process compliance, since a source comment asserting a process happened is not evidence and the reviewer was right to say so.

rounds.question: The grill found my "question stays exactly as typed" claim is already false: use-ask.ts:86 stores the TRIMMED input on the turn, so leading/trailing whitespace is dropped the moment anyone asks anything. What should the guarantee actually be?
options: Narrow the claim to what's true (Recommended)
